title: Portrait container uses stretch anchors causing 130px tall rect for 60px portrait

title: Phase 7: Implement neutral/colorless abilities (8 abilities)
description:
Implement ~8 abilities available to all archetypes regardless of choice. These fill gaps and provide universally useful options.

**Adrenaline** (Common, 3 bindings) — Active, attack or defense. Draw 2 cards immediately. One use per match. Simple, always useful.

**Endurance** (Passive, Uncommon, 0 bindings) — +1 max hand size for the match. Permanent hand advantage.

**Adaptable** (Passive, Common, 0 bindings) — Your first defense each bout can use any card of equal or higher rank regardless of suit (not just trump/matching suit). Defensive flexibility.

**Second Wind** (Common, 3 bindings) — Active, defense. After eating (triggered automatically), draw 1 extra card from deck. Softens eating penalty.

**Last Stand** (Passive, Uncommon, 0 bindings) — When your hand is 2 or fewer cards, defenses can use any suit (like Endgame Specialist but hand-size based instead of deck-size).

**Counterspell** (Rare, 1 binding) — Active, attack or defense. Cancel the ability that was just activated by opponent this bout. Reactive counter-play.

**Resourceful** (Passive, Uncommon, 0 bindings) — When you win a bout as defender (opponent discards), draw 1 extra card. Rewards solid defense.

**Tempo** (Common, 3 bindings) — Active, attack. If bout is empty (first attack), your first 2 attacks this bout don't need rank matching (like DoubleTrouble but for opening). Sets tempo for the bout.

Reclassify some existing abilities as neutral: ExtraDraw, Blocker, SeizeInitiative move to neutral pool. DoubleDefense, TrumpAffinity, EndgameSpecialist, QuickHands also stay neutral.
close_reason: Phases 3-7: all build paths implemented, compiled, tested

title: Implement Gambler Trickster build path (5 abilities)
description:
Implement 5 abilities for the Gambler Trickster build path (deception/hidden information). All use/generate Luck resource.

**Bluff** (Common, 3 bindings) — Active ability during attack. Play a card face-down as an attack. Opponent must either defend blind (play a card that would beat it IF revealed) or eat. If opponent successfully defends, they see the card. If they eat, the bluff card returns to your hand. Generates 1 Luck.

**Misdirection** (Uncommon, 2 bindings) — Active ability during attack. Swap one of your already-played attack cards on the table with a different card from your hand. The new card must be a legal attack. This can invalidate an opponent's defense (they defended the old card, new card might be higher). Costs 1 Luck.

**Wild Card** (Uncommon, 2 bindings) — Active ability during attack or defense. Play any card as if it were any suit of your choice (rank stays the same). One use per bout. Costs 2 Luck. Extremely flexible — turns any card into a trump-suit card for defense or changes suit for attack.

**Read the Room** (Passive, 0 bindings) — At the start of each bout, see opponent's highest-rank card and lowest-rank card (but not their full hand). Generates 1 Luck per bout. Information advantage without full reveal.

**Three Card Monte** (Rare, 1 binding) — Active ability during defense. Shuffle 3 cards from your hand face-down. Opponent's AI (or human choice) picks one to discard from your hand. BUT you arrange the 3 cards — you know which is which. Against AI: the AI picks randomly; you can put your worst card in the most likely pick position. Mind game ability. Costs 2 Luck.
close_reason: All 52 new abilities implemented, compiled, tested

title: Implement Gambler High Roller build path (5 abilities)
description:
Implement 5 abilities for the Gambler High Roller build path (risk/reward via Luck). All use/generate Luck resource.

**Double Down** (Common, 3 bindings) — Active ability during defense. Voluntarily eat all current attacks (don't try to defend). Gain 3 Luck. Next bout when you attack, your attacks ignore rank-match rules. High risk (eating cards) for high reward (free attacks). Engine needs _doubleDownActive flag.

**Jackpot** (Rare, 1 binding) — Active ability during attack or defense. Requires Luck >= 5. Draw 3 extra cards immediately. Costs all current Luck (resets to 0). The big payoff for accumulating Luck.

**Snake Eyes** (Uncommon, 2 bindings) — Active ability during attack. Flip (reveal) the top deck card. If rank <= 8 (Six through Eight), opponent must eat immediately (bout ends). If rank > 8 (Nine through Ace), YOU must eat instead. Pure gambling. Generates 2 Luck regardless of outcome.

**House Edge** (Passive, 0 bindings) — When you eat (take cards), 50% chance (coin flip using engine RNG) to draw 1 extra card from deck. Softens the penalty of eating, synergizes with Double Down. Generates 1 Luck per trigger.

**All or Nothing** (Rare, 1 binding) — Active ability during attack. Stake the bout: if you win this bout (opponent eats), they eat DOUBLE cards (each attack counts twice for eating purposes). If you lose (you eat or bout ends in defense), YOU eat double instead. Costs 3 Luck. The ultimate gamble.

Double Defense — activate when facing 2+ undefended attacks and the card can cover both.

title: Implement Tier 2 abilities: Blocker, Seize Initiative, Double Trouble, Double Defense
description: Four abilities that modify bout rules. The Blocker (defense): sets a flag on the bout preventing the attacker from adding more cards this bout. Seize Initiative (either phase): sets a flag so the activating player becomes attacker after bout resolves, regardless of defense outcome. Double Trouble (attack): grants one additional attack this bout that ignores the rank-match constraint. Double Defense (defense): the played card covers the current undefended slot AND the next one, if both attacks can be beaten by this card's rank or suit.
design: Bout gets new flags: AttacksCapped (for Blocker), and a slot for 'double defense covers two'. GameEngine.ResolveBout checks a SeizeInitiative override for attacker selection. Double Trouble temporarily relaxes CanAttackWith for one play. These are the most complex abilities — each modifies a different part of the rules pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: All four abilities function correctly for human and AI. Edge cases tested: Blocker when attacker has no follow-ups (no-op), Double Defense when only one attack exists (covers just one), Seize Initiative when activator already would have been attacker (no-op), Double Trouble when no legal follow-up rank exists (the extra attack can be any rank).
close_reason: All 4 Tier 2 abilities implemented. Blocker: caps attacks via Bout.AttacksCapped. Seize Initiative: overrides attacker selection in ResolveBout. Double Trouble: rank bypass flag consumed on next TryAttack. Double Defense: card defends first slot + auto-defends second slot. Bout extended with AutoDefend/AttacksCapped. Validated, smoke test passes.

value: unity-mcp bridge (com.unity.ai.assistant relay) drops when Unity does a domain reload (Play mode entry while compiling, or RunCommand crashes inside Unity). Doesn't auto-recover; requires /mcp reload in Claude Code. Workaround: wait for compile to fully finish before pressing Play. Time penalty per drop: ~30 seconds + user interaction.

RunManager.StartAutoRun() drives complete roguelike runs without UI interaction. Press R to toggle during non-match phases. Uses Time.timeScale=20 and AiThinkSeconds=0.02f for fast execution. Auto-selects map nodes (Match > Elite > Rest > Rumor > Shop priority). GameManager.SetAutoPlay(true) enables match auto-play. Stall detection in GameManager.Update forces TryEat after 100 stalled frames.

Unity MCP RunCommand breaks silently when code uses System.Reflection (e.g. Enum.GetValues, Type.GetMethod). The bridge disconnects and Debug.Log output disappears. Workaround: call [MenuItem] methods via ManageMenuItem for reflection-heavy code, or inline logic without reflection in RunCommand. Rule added to CLAUDE.md.

Wits&Fools: GameLoop initially Pumped() synchronously inside OnAttackPlayed handler, which caused AI to act before GameManager's visual handler ran (subscriber order). Refactored to GameLoop.Tick() called per-frame from GameManager.Update; AI ticks delayed by AiThinkSeconds for deliberate pacing. Avoids re-entering engine inside its own events.

Wits&Fools engine smoke test: menu 'Wits and Fools/Smoke Test/Play 50 Games (Greedy AIs)' or via Unity_ManageMenuItem. Runs 50 deterministic games with greedy AIs vs each other. Healthy result: 0 stalls (safety cap), roughly balanced wins, avg ~13 turns/game. Prints to Unity console — read with FilterText='Smoke Test'.
